bullets.title: S&P 500 closes at record high; Goldman raises YE target to 8,000 on AI-driven earnings
bullets.body: S&P 500 (+0.61% to 7,519) and Nasdaq (+1.16%) both hit record closing highs on May 26, with 19 ATHs recorded in 2026. Goldman Sachs raised its year-end target to 8,000 (from 7,600) on stronger earnings: $340 EPS +24% YoY in 2026, $385 +13% in 2027, with AI infrastructure beneficiaries expected to drive ~50% of 2026 EPS growth. Futures pre-market +0.18–0.31%, extending the move.

bullets.title: Semiconductors surge: MU and SK Hynix join $1T club; SOX up 5.5% on AI demand
bullets.body: Micron surged 19–22% to cross $1T market cap after UBS tripled its PT to $1,625, citing LTAs with EPS >$100 through 2029E and ~$400B FCF generation. SK Hynix separately eclipsed $1T driven by AI data center demand. The SOX posted its strongest day since April 8 (+5.5%), with MRVL +5.8%, WDC +6.3%, STX +6.3%, AMD +2.0%. Global DRAM revenue neared $100B in Q1 2026. Pre-market SOXX +3.6% and MU +9.0% extending the rally.

bullets.title: ZS -25% post-earnings; FY27 ARR guidance 16–17% vs 21% Street estimate triggers cybersecurity selloff
bullets.body: Zscaler beat F3Q (revenue $850M, +25.4% YoY; ARR $3.53B) but guided FY27 revenue and ARR growth of only 16–17% vs consensus ~19–21%, citing departure of two senior go-to-market leaders and conservative new logo assumptions. FY26 FCF margin was cut to ~23% from ~27% on pulled-forward capex. The print triggered sympathy selling across cybersecurity: PANW -4.8%, CRWD -4.3%, NET -3.1%, FTNT -4.4% pre-market. Multiple banks cut PTs (Evercore to $155, Piper to $160, Truist to $200) while bulls (Wolfe, KeyBanc, Citi) maintain Buy noting 5x CY27 revenue is 44% discount to peers.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions drive oil volatility; WTI settles ~$93–94 with peace deal hopes capping downside
bullets.body: WTI settled down ~2.8% at $93.89 on May 26 on US-Iran peace talk optimism, with further pre-market weakness to $90.33 (-3.6%). Iran's IRGC claims 'intelligent control' over the strait with 25 ships transiting, while Dallas Fed's Logan warned a prolonged blockade would require major global consumption cuts and Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari flagged multiple rate hike risks if the conflict persists. Energy sector underperforms in Europe/US while refining names (PSX, PARR) upgraded by Mizuho.

bullets.title: NVDA plans $150B annual Taiwan investment; TSMC eyes 15% 3nm price hike in 2H26
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced plans to spend up to $150B per year on Taiwan AI suppliers, calling the island the 'epicentre' of the AI revolution — up from $10–15B four years ago. TSMC is reportedly planning a ~15% price hike on 3nm wafers in 2H26 due to severe capacity shortages, with further 5–10% increases in 2027. Infineon announced its second 2026 power semiconductor price hike effective July 1. ByteDance is weighing up to $70B in 2026 AI capex.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades datacenter capex outlook +80% for 2026; memory to consume ~30% of hyperscaler budgets
bullets.body: JPMorgan revised datacenter capex estimates up ~80% for 2026 and ~50% for 2027, implying $250B+ additional spending. Memory is expected to account for ~30% of hyperscaler capex in 2026 (up from ~8% in 2023–24). Hyperscaler 2027 capex revised up from ~$950B to $1.11T as GOOGL, META, AMZN, MSFT, ORCL all expand plans. Alchip Chairman noted 3nm shortages are more severe than memory. Tech is the most bought sector by hedge funds over the past week.

bullets.title: Fed commentary: no near-term hawkish bias; March 2027 hike priced as neutral rate normalization, not tightening
bullets.body: Analysis suggests the rate hike priced in for March 2027 reflects a higher neutral rate rather than a genuinely hawkish Fed bias — actual bias would require several 0.3%+ core inflation prints over summer to shift the 2026 forecast to 3.5%. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow is tracking +3.3% core GDP growth in Q2, well above the 2% threshold for restrictive policy. Riskiest factors (earnings volatility, leverage, momentum) would underperform in a true hawkish scenario but are not doing so currently.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury touches two-week lows; oil-driven disinflation reduces aggressive tightening bets
bullets.body: The US 10-year yield touched a two-week low in Asian trade (tracking ~4.44%), with Hedgeye flagging the break below 4.44% after macro tourists called for rising yields. JPM forecasts the 10Y stays in a 4.40–4.60% range in June, ending at 4.40%. Falling oil prices reduced inflation concerns and pushed traders to scale back expectations for aggressive Fed action. SPY, QQQ, and Russell 2000 all hit all-time highs.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples expanding: All-SaaS index +4.2% WoW, All-Security +8.5% WoW; key prints tonight CRM, MRVL
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.0x FY+2 EV/Sales after +4.2% multiple expansion last week; the All-Security index saw +8.5% WoW expansion to 7.3x. Despite ZS pressure on cybersecurity, the broader security software cohort is up ~40% over the past month. Key earnings tonight: CRM (est. $3.13 EPS / $11.05B revenue), MRVL ($0.80 EPS / $2.41B revenue). SNOW, MDB, ADSK, BRZE also due this week.

bullets.title: GOOGL scores 10/10 in JPM sentiment matrix — first Internet stock ever; MSFT becoming funding short
bullets.body: Google became the first stock to achieve 10/10 in JPMorgan's tech sentiment matrix, driven by its full-stack AI positioning and Search/Gemini convergence. MSFT is increasingly cited as a funding short despite quality large-cap status. SPOT is now 'King of Media' post-investor day, NFLX is a funding short with anemic engagement growth, and APP surged 7% after an Edgewater note suggested META is unlikely to pursue non-IDFA bidding on iOS before 2027 at earliest.

bullets.title: NVDA cash return doubling to $111B could add 50bps to S&P 500 total return ratio
bullets.body: Nvidia plans to return ~50% of free cash flow to shareholders, roughly doubling its cash return from $54B to $111B on a trailing twelve-month basis. If hyperscaler AI spending flows to chipmakers, energy, and data center companies that increase their own cash returns, the S&P 500 cash return ratio could rebound materially — the ratio currently sits at its lowest level since the GFC. If cash return stays at Q4 levels permanently, S&P 500 fair value is estimated 12% lower.

bullets.title: JPM tactically bullish; June seasonality +1.85% avg with 90% hit rate; rotation broadening into cyclicals
bullets.body: JPM maintains a Tactically Bullish stance and recommends a shift toward Quality names within Tech given potential for higher yields. June has returned +1.85% on average with a 90% hit rate over the past 10 years (July: +3.37%, 100%). Momentum/Bonds saw inflows while Materials/Utilities/EM/Crypto saw outflows. Geopolitical risk easing on a potential US-Iran deal is supporting cyclical broadening; JPM notes broadening into Physical AI plays including China/Japan with Korea/Taiwan outperforming.

bullets.title: Consumer spending tracking solid: Chase data shows +5.1% YoY MTD; upper/mid income +6.7%
bullets.body: JPMorgan Chase card data through May 14 shows consumer spending +5.1% YoY MTD: Upper/Middle Income +6.7%, Lower Income +4.8%. Non-discretionary spending +5.8% vs discretionary +4.8%, with gasoline/energy +25.8% YoY. Credit card delinquency and household debt service ratios remain below historical averages. May retail traffic decelerated (Citi tracker: Wk3 +0.4% vs Wk2 +1.1%) while May MTD Citi card retail spending accelerated to +1.8% in Week 3 vs +0.7% in Week 2.

bullets.title: MedTech trading at 25-year relative lows vs S&P 500; PE and activist creating floor
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes MedTech is down ~30% vs S&P 500 YTD, one of the worst 15-20 year stretches. Piper Sandler confirms the sector is at 25-year relative lows vs the S&P 500, with volumes steady and innovation robust. Three catalysts for reversal: significant share repurchases, full rebasing of forward expectations, and visibility into positive growth catalysts. Private equity and activists are rapidly acquiring mis-priced assets. Most dislocated names cited: ISRG, BSX, STE, MMSI, ATRC.

bullets.title: Asia energy supercycle: $5T+ capex through 2030, data centers to consume 1/6th of new Asian power units
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Asia energy blueprint projects annual energy investment reaching $1.3T by 2030 (vs $860B in 2025, 11% CAGR), driven by AI data centers, coal gasification, storage, and nuclear. Data centers will consume roughly one-sixth of all new power units in Asia by 2030. The firm identifies $9T in enterprise value creation potential across the energy value chain and a 70-stock global equity shortlist including Mitsui, Venture Global, CATL, Keppel, Kansai Electric, Cummins, and Doosan.

bullets.title: Wolfe May payrolls preview: +105k vs 95k consensus; wages +0.34% MoM; downside surprise more market-moving
bullets.body: Wolfe forecasts May nonfarm payrolls at +105k (above the 95k Bloomberg consensus), with private payrolls at +110k and government -5k. Average hourly earnings are projected at +0.34% MoM (+3.5% YoY), with unemployment edging up to 4.39%. Cyclical sectors show recovery signs while AI-impacted sectors continue to shed jobs. Given hawkish Fed and strong growth narratives, a downside payrolls surprise would have more market impact than an upside one.

bullets.title: EU approves tariff cuts on US goods; US confirms Mexico/Canada tariffs remain; USTR rejects exclusion programs
bullets.body: EU governments cleared legislation to implement import duty cuts on US goods as part of the EU-US trade agreement. Separately, a US official confirmed tariffs on Mexico and Canada will remain in place. USTR Greer stated the Trump administration is not interested in tariff exclusion programs, with Section 301 investigations to seek public comments on proposed measures.

bullets.title: Power semiconductor supply crunch deepening: Infineon 2nd price hike of 2026; passive component orders suspended
bullets.body: Infineon announced its second power semiconductor price hike of 2026 effective July 1, with the company described as the world's largest power semi maker. China's Fenghua Advanced Technology suspended order intake for 0402/0603 chip resistors and MLCC product lines due to surging volumes. Laminate and board material prices are up 10–20%. These supply signals are consistent with AI infrastructure and data center build-out driving broad electronic component demand.

bullets.title: IREN +3.9% pre-market on $1.6B Dell Blackwell air-cooled system purchase agreement
bullets.body: Iris Energy entered a $1.6B purchase agreement with Dell for air-cooled Blackwell GPU systems, driving IREN +3.9% pre-market. The deal adds to broader AI infrastructure buildout signals and is consistent with multiple reports of Dell Blackwell demand strength.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD merger set for DOJ approval; Morgan Stanley double-upgrades PSKY to Overweight
bullets.body: The DOJ is expected to approve Paramount's ~$110B acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery after CEO David Ellison reaffirmed theatrical release commitments to regulators. Paramount is targeting a July 15 close, with a $0.25/share quarterly ticking fee if not closed by Sept 30. Morgan Stanley double-upgraded PSKY to Overweight, named FWONK its top pick in a 'Live 5' media basket, and is bullish on EQIX as a top pick among data center REITs on an 'Inference Inflection' thesis.
